articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt the financial networks of those who support illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations, reinforcing the U.S. commitment to combating these threats globally.
Further details on the specific individuals and entities designated, and the implications of these designations, are available on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for Apparent Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Bank of America, N.A. for apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs.
The settlement addresses the bank's alleged failures to comply with U.S. sanctions regulations, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
This action underscores OFAC's continued focus on enforcing sanctions compliance within the financial sector and holding institutions accountable for lapses in their programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, International Criminal Court Designation, and Burma-related Removal
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics for apparent sanctions violations. This action is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions programs.

In a separate but concurrent action, OFAC also announced a designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and issued associated General Licenses. Additionally, a Burma-related designation has been removed.
These diverse actions highlight OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, addressing various threats and adjusting designations as circumstances evolve.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new Russia-related General License.
This new General License provides authorization for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.

The issuance of General Licenses often indicates specific carve-outs or humanitarian considerations within broader sanctions regimes, aiming to mitigate unintended consequences while maintaining pressure on the targeted country.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations, Issues New Iran General License and Amended Russia General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, further expanding sanctions against entities and individuals connected to the Iranian regime.

Concurrently, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License, which may permit certain transactions previously prohibited, and an amended Russia-related General License, indicating adjustments to existing authorizations.
These actions reflect a continued strategy of applying targeted pressure on Iran while also making specific adjustments to sanctions programs concerning both Iran and Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals, Updates, and Publishes Iran-related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several designations removals and updates, indicating a dynamic approach to its sanctions lists.

In addition, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert, warning foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted without advance notice if they continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.
An amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) was also published, providing further clarification on existing regulations and policies regarding Iran sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism activities.
These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks and support structures of terrorist organizations, reinforcing global efforts to combat terrorism.
The action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to protecting national security by isolating those who facilitate or engage in terrorist acts.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations and Updates, Designates Transnational Criminal Organization, and Publishes Iran-related Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and designations updates, further tightening sanctions on the Iranian regime.
In a separate action, OFAC also designated a Transnational Criminal Organization, highlighting efforts to combat illicit financial activities globally.
Additionally, an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) were published, providing further guidance and clarification on existing sanctions policies.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism and transnational criminal organizations.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced the removal of several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics activities, and Libya.
These actions demonstrate OFAC's ongoing efforts to adapt its sanctions programs to current threats and geopolitical developments, adding new targets while delisting others.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a broad set of new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics, counter terrorism, Iran-related activities, and non-proliferation efforts.
This comprehensive action underscores the U.S. government's multi-faceted approach to combating a range of illicit activities that threaten national security and foreign policy interests.
The designations aim to disrupt the financial networks supporting these activities and reinforce international norms against such conduct.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
